correctness.rationale: The Gaussian exponential identity Im E exp((k+2πi)Z)=exp((k²-4π²)/2)sin(2πk)=0 for each nonnegative integer k proves μ+ and μ− are normalized nonnegative distinct lognormal Stieltjes laws with identical moments m_k=exp(k²/2). The shared fair latent sign S makes each row conditionally iid, and E(Y^k|S)=m_k; total variance is the conditional kth-power variance averaged over S divided by n, O_k(n^-1). Finite R truncated Ψ_R is a polynomial and every marginal has all finite moments, so a single K bounds the norm across rows. Conditional iid empirical convergence in expected W1 holds by finite first moment. The reverse triangle inequality then gives the exact limit E W1(μ_n,μbar)=W1(μ+,μ−)/2>0 because μbar=(μ++μ−)/2 and the one-dimensional CDF W1 formula. The claim does not cover independent unconditionally observed rows nor growing R.

value.rationale: A precise, natural necessity boundary for an assumption in a current dependent-data empirical-Wasserstein theorem: uniformly controlling any fixed tail-moment order cannot replace controlled orders tending to infinity in the absence of determinacy. The result is not a free-floating toy obstruction: it preserves every fixed empirical-moment variance bound and gives a computable positive limiting transport gap. It does not claim the growing-order condition is individually necessary when other hypotheses are added.
